title: Session Gradient Gambit — playbook sketch
content:
Context / motivation:
- Working on a light-weight, deterministic way to trade latency/cost vs. answer quality across long-lived user sessions. Current approaches are binary (full-context vs trimmed) or rule-based heuristics that feel brittle across workloads.
- Idea: treat session fidelity as a continuous variable and manage it with small, observable policy changes — a "gradient" rather than hard lanes. Call this approach the Session Gradient Gambit.

Problem statement:
- Many customers have mixed signals: some queries need full fidelity, others are fine with reduced context. Static laneing leads to wasted tokens or poor quality.
- Need a low-risk way to gradually reduce per-request compute for cheap queries while preserving top-tier quality for high-signal moments.

Hypothesis:
- If we apply an annealed fidelity policy (gradually degrade less-important turns using cached heuristics + small model variants), we can reduce token spend by 12–25% on typical chat workloads with <2% quality regression (measured by task-specific evals).

High-level goals (user-centric):
- Maintain conversational coherence for top-priority tasks (commands, transactions)
- Reduce cost on casual chit-chat and background context accumulation
- Provide transparent controls for product teams to set tolerances per journey

Success metrics:
- delta_cost_per_session (target: -15% median)
- quality_regression_rate (target: <2% on eval prompt set)
- rollback_rate (target: <1% of sessions triggering auto-fallback to full fidelity)
- developer_satisfaction (qualitative from 3 pilot teams)

Core components (sketch):
1) Fidelity score per turn: small heuristic model (or light classifier) that outputs a 0..1 fidelity importance score. Uses signals: user intent confidence, presence of task entities, recent edits, explicit tool calls, user role.
2) Annealing scheduler: given a base fidelity target for session, scheduler gradually applies scaled compression (eviction weights, summary windows, prefix drop) as the session length grows or as budget thresholds are approached.
3) Micro-variants / graceful fallbacks: lightweight model variants (quantized, shorter context) that can be swapped in for low-score turns; automatic fallback to base model if coherence drops.
4) Telemetry + gating: per-token cost attribution, rolling evals on held prompt set, circuit-breaker that flips session to full-fidelity on failure patterns.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM for an assistant product, I want casual messages to be cheap so my run-rate stays predictable, while important transactional messages remain high fidelity.
- As an ML engineer, I want an SDK toggle to test annealing schedules and see simulated cost & eval impact per route.
- As SRE, I want circuit-breaker logs and rollup metrics to know when fallbacks are happening at scale.

Design ideas / tactics:
- Two-axis signals: Intent-importance (binary-ish) x Recency-importance (continuous). Priority = f(intent, recency, explicit user tokens).
- Soft-eviction: mark lower-priority turns with a decay timestamp (probabilistic eviction for older turns).
- Summary-on-write: convert long tails to one-shot semantic summaries when fidelity < threshold. Include provenance markers so we can surface "this content summarized" in the UI.
- Time-based anneal: sessions older than X minutes begin progressive trimming unless a high-importance turn resets.
- Hysteresis: make ramps asymmetric (easier to increase fidelity than to shrink further) to avoid oscillation.

Experiments to run (MVP):
- Experiment A: heuristic fidelity classifier + fixed anneal schedule vs control. Measure cost and quality on 100k simulated sessions.
- Experiment B: same as A but with micro-variant fallback enabled and circuit-breaker thresholds tuned.
- Experiment C: UI experiment exposing "economy mode" toggle per user and measuring conversion/engagement.

Implementation constraints / notes:
- Minimal infra footprint: prefer server-side heuristics and existing summary pipeline. Avoid heavy model infra changes for MVP.
- Privacy: opt-out for sensitive sessions; do not persist summaries unencrypted in public logs.
- Observability hooks required in Console: per-session fidelity timeline, token cost attribution, reason codes for eviction.

Open questions / risks:
- How to generate reliable fidelity labels for supervised training? (need a small labeled corpus: manual annotation + heuristics)
- UI communication: when do we surface that older context was summarized/evicted without confusing users?
- Cold-start sessions where system lacks context — do we default to safe full-fidelity for first N turns?

Next steps (short-term):
- Prototype heuristic classifier (features: message length, message type, urgency triggers, tool invocation) — owner: Mira Shah — due: 2025-04-18
- Wire basic annealing scheduler in sim harness and run Experiment A — owner: Devon Patel — due: 2025-05-02
- Define eval prompt set and rollback rules, coordinate with Research for measurement — owner: Evelyn Park — due: 2025-04-25

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep "gambit" reversible — fallbacks should be fast and observable.
- Consider exposing per-turn fidelity hints in debug SDK to help integrators tune.
- Could combine with routing policies (route low-fidelity turns to cheaper region/hardware).
- Add tagging schema for summaries so we can filter by provenance in logs.
